title: Calibration healthcheck & failover policy for quantized deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a deterministic healthcheck and automatic failover strategy for canary deployments of quantized model profiles (FP8/INT8). The controller must validate calibration stability and end-to-end accuracy signals against the float baseline during staged traffic experiments and automatically revert traffic to a safe variant when thresholds are breached.
background: We have seen intermittent regression in hallucination and semantic-match metrics when serving certain model families under INT8/FP8 profiles. Manual rollbacks are slow and error-prone. Prior tickets improved calibration tooling (e.g. ENG-8423) and observability, but we lack an automated, auditable gating mechanism tied to canary traffic and routing policies.
proposal: Extend the rollout controller to run a live calibration healthcheck during canary windows. Healthchecks will compute a daily set of lightweight accuracy and safety signals on an evaluation probe set (semantic match, exact-match, hallucination-rate), latency and token-cost deltas, and KV/cache hit-rate. Define conservative threshold windows (configurable per model family) and implement a failover policy that: 1) immediately drains traffic to the float baseline or last-known-good quant profile, 2) writes an audit event and creates an incident in the rollout timeline, 3) preserves telemetry for post-mortem and replay. Provide a UI in Console to view gate evaluations and to manually override when needed.
tasks: Design probe-set composition and sampling strategy for live canary (PM + MLE)
Add realtime evaluator in serving edge to compute: semantic match, LM perplexity delta, hallucination heuristic, and latency/cost deltas
Implement gating policy in rollout controller with three outcomes: PASS, WARN, FAIL
Wire automatic traffic steering to safe variant + graceful connection draining
Emit audit logs and create standardized incident events for Console timeline
Build Dashboard panels in Console: gate history, probe-set performance, and candidate vs baseline comparisons
Create integration tests that simulate degraded accuracy and verify automated fallback
Run staged experiments on three model families and document thresholds and calibration recipes
acceptance_criteria: When probe-set accuracy drops by more than configured delta for a given model family, traffic is automatically routed away from the quantized candidate within 60s
Audit event and an incident are created automatically with links to the probe-set and a continuous snapshot of telemetry
Console displays gate evaluation results for each canary rollout and exposes a single-click override
Automated integration tests validate fallback behavior end-to-end in CI
Operators can configure separate thresholds per model family and per profile (FP8/INT8) via runtime config

notes: Use conservative default thresholds: accuracy delta -1.5% absolute, hallucination-rate +0.8% absolute. These will be tuned per family.
Fallback targets: prefer last-known-good quant profile if exists; otherwise route to float baseline in same region to avoid cold-start regressions.
Retention: store probe snapshots and gate decisions for 90 days for audit and regression analysis.
